newsitem.title: UK: UK May global trade deficit 508 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: UK May global trade deficit 508 mln stg.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics issued the following data on Britain's global trade in May (in million stg, previously announced data in brackets)
TRADE VALUE EX OIL/ERRATICS May April (Prel Apr)
TRADE IN OIL (VALUE MLN STG) May April (Prel Apr)
Economists had forecast a deficit of 960 million stg.
The ONS said the trend for Britain's global trade gap was narrowing.

May's provisional estimates show both export and import prices little changed compared with April. In the three months to the end of May, both sets of prices fell by one percent, the ONS said. The terms of trade were little changed.

In value terms within the EU a rise in exports to Germany contrasted with a fall in exports to the Irish Republic. Outside the EU, growth in exports to the rest of the world was offset by the drop in export to oil exporting countries.
Total exports in May fell 2.5 percent to 14.1 billion stg. Exports to EU countries fell 1.5 percent while those to non-EU countries fell 4.0 percent.

Total imports in May fell 5.5 percent to 14.6 billion stg. Imports from EU countries fell nine percent while those from non-EU countries dropped 1.5 percent. The ONS said there was no certain evidence of a reaction to the pound's strength.
